notes: Perfect claim overlap (C86, C87, C88, C89) regarding Bip1 processing mutant phenotypes. Both evaluators agree the functional validation data (growth delay, cell death) are well-supported.
High overlap (7/8 claims shared: C135-C141) on evolutionary interpretation. Both agree that S. pombe represents novel diversity in UPR mechanisms using conserved machinery in unexpected ways.
High overlap (5/6 claims: C10, C83, C84, C85, C121) on Bip1 translation. Both agree that polysome profiling, ribosome footprinting, and Western blots support increased translation of truncated mRNA.
Substantial overlap (11/22 claims: C8, C68-C71, C75-C78, C82, C116) on Bip1 mRNA processing. Both evaluators agree this novel 3' UTR processing mechanism is well-characterized and unique to S. pombe.
Moderate overlap (3/8 claims: C5, C6, C90) on absence of UPR transcriptional program. Both agree S. pombe lacks Hac1/XBP1 ortholog and uses RIDD rather than transcriptional control.
Moderate overlap (6/16 claims: C7, C43, C45, C48, C49, C50) on RIDD mechanism. Both agree that Ire1-dependent selective mRNA degradation is well-demonstrated and represents a major contribution.

Moderate overlap (6/18 claims: C57-C61, C66) on Ire1 cleavage specificity. Both accept the endonucleolytic mechanism and sequence specificity, though peer reviewers suggest additional Xrn1Δ experiments would strengthen (not validate) conclusions.

Single shared claim (C92) on 15% reduction in ER protein influx. Both find this quantitative impact puzzling given the lethal phenotype. Peer reviewers propose alternative cis-acting mechanism; LLM notes speculation about qualitative effects.

Limited overlap (3/22 claims: C73, C74, C119) on Bip1 mRNA stabilization. Both agree on the stabilization data where claims overlap, but peer review encompasses broader Bip1 processing claims not in LLM R6.
Limited overlap (3/22 claims: C79, C80, C81) on Bip1 cleavage site mutations. Both agree on mutational validation data, but peer review R4 covers much broader Bip1 processing mechanism.

Limited overlap (4/17 claims: C62-C65) on reporter constructs and substrate recognition. Both agree on ORF sequence sufficiency and mutational analysis, but peer R3 focuses more on cleavage mechanism while LLM R4 emphasizes recognition model.

Minimal overlap (1/17 claims: C54) on transient cleavage product accumulation. LLM finds speculation about coupling to clearance uncertain; peer review accepts broader endonucleolytic mechanism as supported.
Claims C105-C108, C110 on substrate recognition determinants only evaluated by LLM. LLM notes that additional determinants beyond UGC motif remain incompletely specified.
Claims C120, C125-C127 on tBip1 mRNA stability mechanism only evaluated by LLM. LLM finds RNA degron and 2'-O-methylation hypotheses speculative and untested.
Claims C142-C147 on RIDD as ancestral state only evaluated by LLM. LLM notes this evolutionary speculation is explicitly acknowledged as unproven by authors.
Claim C11 on evolutionary diversity only in peer review R8. Peer reviewers accept this as revealing 'novel and unexpected diversity' in UPR management (overlaps conceptually with LLM R14).
